CHIEF COMPLAINT
Post-operative follow-up after bilateral reduction mammoplasty.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
36-year-old female presenting for post-operative evaluation following bilateral reduction mammoplasty performed on 10-10-2020. Patient reports breasts are doing well. She denies experiencing chills, fever, nausea, or vomiting. She reports resolution of back pain that she had been experiencing previously. Patient notes she felt a lump under her left breast when she was seen by PA Ruth Sanchez in March, but has not felt it since then after performing massages. She has been using scar gel daily for scar management. On examination, bilateral incisions are well-healed with no signs of infection or redness. Scars are noted to be slightly widened, particularly in one area with high tension. Patient reports the scars are bothering her somewhat, particularly one area. No hard spots, lumps, or bumps currently appreciated on examination.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Denies chills, fever, nausea, or vomiting. No acute complaints other than cosmetic concerns regarding scars.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Bilateral reduction mammoplasty performed 10-10-2020.

MEDICATIONS
Mederma scar gel.

ALLERGIES
Not discussed.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not discussed.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient reports enjoying summertime. Family doing well.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Bilateral breasts examined. Incisions well-healed with no signs of infection or redness. Scars noted to be slightly widened in areas, particularly in one high-tension area. No hard spots, lumps, or bumps appreciated.

RESULTS
Clinical photographs obtained for documentation and follow-up comparison.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Post-operative bilateral reduction mammoplasty with excellent healing and no concerning findings. Continue Mederma scar gel twice daily and massage to scars. Patient to return in six months for re-evaluation of scars. Discussed that scar revision would typically not be considered until at least one year post-operatively. Plan to revisit in six months and reassess scars at that time.
